title: Startup, Memory & Faults
description: Review of startup, the memory map and linker script, stack and heap use, non-volatile storage, fault handling, and the watchdog.

items.text: Startup code initializes .data and .bss, clocks, and the FPU before main
items.hint: Review vendor startup files rather than trusting them. Check the vector table location.

items.text: The reset cause is read, logged, and cleared at every boot
items.hint: Power-on, brownout, watchdog, software, or pin reset. It's the first clue to field failures.

items.text: Boot time to a working product is measured and meets the requirement
items.hint: Measure from power applied to outputs ready and the UI responsive.

items.text: Option bytes or fuses are documented and set by the production process
items.hint: Brownout level, boot pins, watchdog hardware start, read protection.

items.text: The linker script matches the part's memory map and the flash partition plan
items.hint: Bootloader, application slots, configuration and storage regions don't overlap.

items.text: The map file is reviewed for size against the budget at each release
items.hint: Track flash and RAM use per build so growth is noticed early.

items.text: Stack sizes are measured at worst case, with margin
items.hint: Stack painting or static analysis per task and for interrupts. Keep at least 25% margin.

items.text: Stack overflow is detected (MPU guard, canary, or RTOS check)
items.hint: An overflow that silently corrupts RAM is the hardest bug to find in the field.

items.text: Dynamic allocation is avoided after startup, or fragmentation is bounded
items.hint: Prefer static or pool allocation. If malloc is used, measure the high-water mark under long runs.

items.text: Variables shared with DMA or the bootloader are placed in named sections
items.hint: So their addresses don't move when unrelated code changes.

items.text: Stored data has a version, a length, and a CRC
items.hint: So the firmware can tell blank, corrupt, and old-format data apart.

items.text: Writes survive power loss at any point without corrupting stored data
items.hint: Double-buffered records or a journaling file system. Test by cutting power during writes.

items.text: Flash or EEPROM wear is estimated over the product's life and within endurance
items.hint: Writes per day × years ÷ wear-leveling factor against the rated cycles.

items.text: Defaults are restored cleanly on a first boot or a factory reset
items.hint: Including what a factory reset must keep (calibration, serial number, keys).

items.text: The file system or log handles a full or failed storage device
items.hint: Logs roll over. Writes report errors instead of hanging.

items.text: A watchdog is enabled in release builds and can't be starved by a single stuck task
items.hint: Feed it only when every monitored task has checked in, not from a timer interrupt.

items.text: Fault handlers (HardFault, bus, or memory faults) capture state for later diagnosis
items.hint: Save the PC, LR, and fault registers to retained RAM or flash, then reset.

items.text: Asserts are defined for release builds (log and reset), not compiled out silently
items.hint: Decide deliberately what an assert does in the field.

items.text: The firmware detects and limits reset loops
items.hint: After N quick resets, fall back to a safe mode or the last good image.

items.text: Brownout detection is set at a level where the flash and the MCU still work
items.hint: Pick the BOR level from the datasheet's flash-write minimum voltage.

items.text: The MPU protects code, stacks, and peripherals where the core has one
items.hint: At least a guard region below each stack and no-execute on RAM.
